1) game.js:299-313 PMREMGenerator sky bake + Poly Haven RGBELoader HDR upgrade (~15 lines, environment reflections/ambient). MECHANISM CHOSEN: RenderSettings.defaultReflectionMode/customReflection (a single GLOBAL non-spatial cubemap), not a Reflection Probe GameObject. Reasoning: a Reflection Probe captures surrounding SCENE geometry from a point in space — that is solving a problem the three.js code never has, since PMREMGenerator.fromScene(envScene) bakes a flat, scene-less sky environment (envScene contains only the Sky mesh, nothing else), not a self-reflection of the city. RenderSettings' global reflection slot is the literal match: ONE environment source feeding every PBR material in the scene, exactly like three.js's scene.environment. Implementation ports BOTH of the JS's two stages: stage 1 (game.js:299-306, bake-from-procedural-sky) is DefaultReflectionMode.Skybox, which sources IBL from whatever SetupSkybox() just assigned to RenderSettings.skybox — 'bake whatever the sky looks like right now', done the Unity-native way instead of literally PMREM-baking a throwaway scene (Unity's skybox-sourced reflection IS that bake, performed by the pipeline). Stage 2 (game.js:308-313, the async Poly Haven upgrade) is DefaultReflectionMode.Custom with customReflection set to the Poly Haven HDR, now imported as a real Cubemap — new Editor/EnvironmentReflectionSetup.cs flips Assets/Art/Textures/env.hdr's TextureImporter from the plain Texture2D/equirect import it shipped with (textureShape=Texture2D) to textureShape=TextureCube + generateCubemap=Cylindrical (the correct unwrap for an equirectangular .hdr), done through the typed TextureImporter API and SaveAndReimport() — not hand-edited YAML enum integers, so nothing was guessed. Verified by reading the REAL reimported asset back: AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath<Cubemap> returns non-null, dimension=Cube, size=1024 (ENVREFLECT path=Assets/Art/Textures/env.hdr shape=TextureCube cubemapMode=Cylindrical loaded=Cubemap dimension=Cube size=1024). The one honest simplification: three.js's upgrade is ASYNC (network fetch, applied some frames later); Unity ships env.hdr in the build, so Core/SceneEnvironmentSetup.SetupEnvironmentReflections() reaches the Custom/HDR end state immediately once EnvCubemap is assigned — same end state, no network latency to reproduce.

2) game.js:365-406 N8AOPass + UnrealBloomPass + OutputPass composer (~42 lines), split per the brief's own instruction:
   - Bloom (game.js:397-402): PORTED as a Bloom VolumeComponent override added directly to Assets/DefaultVolumeProfile.asset (new sub-asset block, fileID 11400003, added to the SAME profile Tonemapping/ColorAdjustments already live on — not a new/replacement profile), the same 'static asset, because the JS never changes these after construction' precedent as the existing Tonemapping/ColorAdjustments entries. Values carried across as literals, same units-differ-but-number-carries precedent as SunIntensity: threshold=0.9, intensity=0.14 (UnrealBloomPass's 'strength'), scatter=0.5 (its 'radius'). Two fields are a DIRECT mechanical match, not just a visual one: downscale=Quarter mirrors the JS's own bloom target sized at (w/4,h/4), and highQualityFiltering=false mirrors the JS's plain bilinear setSize-halving blur (not the bicubic upsample that flag turns on). clamp/tint/filter/dirtTexture/dirtIntensity/maxIterations left at URP defaults — UnrealBloomPass has no equivalent knobs for any of them. OutputPass (game.js:403) was NOT separately claimed: URP's own camera render path always performs an equivalent final output/colorspace blit, so there is nothing left to port once Bloom's Volume override exists.
   - N8AO ambient occlusion (game.js:369-391, ~23 lines): NOT PORTED, left exactly as the prior pass flagged it. URP's equivalent is SSAO as a Renderer Feature on the ScriptableRendererData asset (Assets/Settings/TbilisiFly_Renderer.asset) — riskier asset surgery than a Volume override (it edits the renderer's feature LIST, a different asset shape, shared by every system that renders through that renderer) and this pass declines to guess at its YAML shape rather than risk breaking the renderer asset every other Core/City/Flight/Combat system depends on. Flagged as a follow-up requiring either the Renderer Feature's typed C# API in an Editor script (same discipline as EnvironmentReflectionSetup.cs's TextureImporter approach) or manual verification against a known-good SSAO-enabled ScriptableRendererData, not attempted here.
